Ituri: 10 of 31 rings unopened, 7 of 28 households and 2 of 14 facilities not decontaminated, 22 EDS failed, 18 of 71 bodies (25.4%) not swabbed and 10 EDS postponed; Nord-Kivu: 8 of 21 rings unopened (notably Katwa), 9 of 15 households not decontaminated, no household kits (0/6), 2 frontline workers infected in Mabalako, 57 EDS postponed and one body not swabbed at Musienene because of family resistance; Tshopo: 9 bodies not swabbed in the absence of families, with IPC supplies and IPC-trained providers short; Bas-Uele: no EDS done, 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage, 17 of 20 without 72-hour water storage and only 130 of 632 providers (20.6%) trained in IPC-WASH.
Ituri: blood supply short of CTE and hospital needs, 10 patients in Mandima (7 at CT Mandima, 3 at CT Makeke) without food and ambulance movement reporting 16/33.
Nord-Kivu: suspect beds 90.6% occupied (174/192), 148 of 488 hospitalized patients (30.3%) cared for outside CTE/CT, and data completeness 93% (Musienene missing).
Tshopo: 4 confirmed patients who escaped from the CT in Bafwasende are still not found, and food and nutrition support is still to be consolidated with Caritas arriving in Bafwasende.

Bas-Uele: the standard CTE at HGR Buta is delayed, 57 suspects are isolated in health facilities without nutrition support, there is no ambulance and psychosocial support for its 3 confirmed cases is delayed; Haut-Uele's care data for the day did not arrive.

Ituri frontline-worker vaccination stays suspended pending national research committee validation (actors were briefed to resume it in Bunia and Mongbwalu); Nord-Kivu's vaccine stock is exhausted (0 doses left) while coverage stays low (8.4% in Beni, against a provincial target of 36070 frontline workers in 15 zones) and ARKTEK transport remains to be confirmed with WHO; Bas-Uele cold-chain units are not running. Vaccine logistics do not establish efficacy against Bundibugyo.

Triage and isolation areas are insufficient and service use, notably maternity, has fallen in the facilities visited in Tshopo; Bas-Uele antenatal attendance was 58% in August and routine vaccination drop-outs are reported at Rubi-Lisanga; Bas-Uele's MASHAKO 3.0 review shows routine vaccination coverage falling since August 2026; a Nord-Kivu hospital assessment found PPE, hand gel and TB/HIV medicines short and 15 of 122 providers exposed.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 15 of 28 affected zones (53.6%) and 11 of the 43 latest confirmed cases (25.6%) are not yet supported, with coverage around community deaths to strengthen in Nia-Nia; Nord-Kivu coverage around the latest cases stays low in nine zones and 10 affected zones have no creche; Bas-Uele's support for its 3 confirmed cases is still delayed and Haut-Uele's data did not arrive.

Ituri community engagement reporting completeness is low (13 of 28 zones, 46.4%), partly because of a strike in Bunia zone, with 6 of 11 incidents resolved (54.5%); Nord-Kivu received 383 of 650 expected community alerts (58.9%), resolved 3 of 9 incidents (33.3%) and engaged 2448 of 4750 people (51.5%).

Ituri: community reluctance and resistance persist in Mongbwalu and Nyankunde; Tshopo: a confirmed patient on the run is still not found and the body of case 71 was taken by the family before the EDS; Bas-Uele's diesel stock is exhausted while the Buta CTE is built.
